beats.label: S1 · A boy on the beach
beats.text: Eleven-year-old Danny Latimer is found dead below the Broadchurch cliffs. New DI Alec Hardy — hired over local DS Ellie Miller — leads the murder inquiry.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the crime, the town, and the Hardy–Miller partnership that anchors everything after.

beats.label: S1 · Mark's lies
beats.text: Danny's father Mark lies about his whereabouts; his prints turn up in Danny's blood in a clifftop hut, and Beth learns his real alibi was an affair with Becca Fisher.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Puts Mark at the top of the suspect list and detonates the Latimer marriage — the family arc that carries into next season.

beats.label: S1 · Every neighbour a suspect
beats.text: Suspicion moves house to house — Jack Marshall's old conviction, Susan Wright's secrets, Paul Coates's drinking, Nigel Carter's temper. Every neighbour is a possibility.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The paranoia engine of the season: no one in Broadchurch is above suspicion, which is what the killer will hide behind.

beats.label: S1 · The town turns on Jack
beats.text: Journalist Karen White pushes Olly to publish Jack's history; a mob forms, his car is vandalised, and Jack kills himself. Coates accuses the town of failing an innocent man.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moral scar of the season — the community destroyed the wrong man, and the guilt of it defines Broadchurch afterwards.

beats.label: S1 · The boat and the phone
beats.text: Forensics link Danny to the burnt boat; Susan reveals her son Nigel dumped the body on the beach. His alibi holds, but Danny's missing smartphone is suddenly switched on nearby.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Physical evidence narrows the case from the whole town to a single household — the last step before the killer is exposed.

beats.label: S1 · The signal to Ellie's house
beats.text: Hardy traces the phone signal to the Miller house. Interviewing Ellie's son Tom, he learns Tom and Danny had fallen out — but the phone was never Tom's.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The moment the investigation crosses the line into Ellie's own home, setting up the reveal.

beats.label: S1 · Joe confesses
beats.text: Ellie's husband Joe confesses to grooming Danny at the summer house and strangling him when Danny threatened to tell. Ellie attacks Joe in the cell and moves out with her sons.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The reveal that reframes the whole season and detonates Ellie's life — every thread going forward hangs off this.

cliffhanger.text: Joe Miller is in a cell awaiting trial for Danny's murder, having confessed to strangling the boy after grooming him. Ellie's marriage has collapsed, the Latimers are staring down a court case, and Hardy is leaving Broadchurch with the earlier Sandbrook killings still unsolved.
questions: Will Joe's confession actually hold up in court?
Can Ellie stay in Broadchurch — or in the police — after what her husband did?
What really happened to the girls at Sandbrook?

characters.name: Alec Hardy
characters.line: DI who solved Danny's murder; seriously ill, disgraced by his failed Sandbrook case, and planning to leave Broadchurch.

characters.name: Ellie Miller
characters.line: DS whose own husband turned out to be the killer; has taken her sons out of the family home and into a hotel.

characters.name: Joe Miller
characters.line: Ellie's husband; confessed to grooming Danny and strangling him when the boy threatened to tell, now in custody.

characters.name: Beth Latimer
characters.line: Danny's mother; pregnant with a new baby and in fragile reconciliation with Mark after his affair.

characters.name: Mark Latimer
characters.line: Danny's father; grieving, publicly exposed as an adulterer, trying to hold his family together.

characters.name: Tom Miller
characters.line: Ellie's older son and Danny's former friend; wiped messages and files off his phone the day Danny died.

characters.name: Karen White
characters.line: National reporter who came to Broadchurch chasing Hardy's downfall and stayed to cover Danny's case.

characters.name: Paul Coates
characters.line: Town priest with a drinking history who conducted Danny's funeral and named the town's guilt over Jack.

beats.label: S2 · Not Guilty
beats.text: Joe Miller stuns Broadchurch by pleading not guilty to Danny's murder, forcing a trial the town thought it had been spared.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The plea is the engine of the entire season; without it there is no trial and no fallout.

beats.label: S2 · Rival Silks
beats.text: The Latimers recruit retired QC Jocelyn Knight to prosecute; Joe hires her estranged protégée Sharon Bishop to defend him.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets up the courtroom rivalry that shapes every subsequent legal beat.

beats.label: S2 · Sandbrook Returns
beats.text: Hardy reveals he stayed in Broadchurch to protect Claire, key witness in his old Sandbrook child-murder case, and her ex Lee Ashworth follows her to town.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces the parallel Sandbrook plot and the triangle of Hardy, Claire and Lee that drives half the season.

beats.label: S2 · Case Unravels
beats.text: Ellie's earlier assault on Joe gets his confession thrown out, and Bishop paints her and Hardy as lovers who framed him. The prosecution's spine collapses.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Explains why a seemingly solid case ends the way it does; the assault is Ellie's ongoing shame.

beats.label: S2 · Claire's Lies
beats.text: Ellie spots Pippa's stolen pendant in a photo of Claire, and Hardy pieces together that Claire, not Lee, is the true architect of the Sandbrook murders.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Flips the Sandbrook villainy from Lee to Claire, which is the resolution the finale delivers.

beats.label: S2 · Verdict and Truth
beats.text: The jury acquits Joe. Hardy arrests Claire and then Lee, and Ricky Gillespie confesses to killing his niece Lisa in a jealous rage.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The twin resolutions: Broadchurch loses its case, Sandbrook is finally solved.

beats.label: S2 · Banished
beats.text: Mark and Nige kidnap the freed Joe; Ellie and Beth confront him at the beach house and force him to leave Broadchurch forever. Hardy, penance done, prepares to go too.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the exact status quo the next season opens on: Joe gone, community fractured, Hardy leaving.

cliffhanger.text: Joe walks free from court and is then run out of town by the Latimers and Millers, denied any real justice. Hardy, his Sandbrook debt paid, packs to leave a Broadchurch that has been given no closure at all.
questions: Can a town denied a verdict ever move on?
What happens to Ellie and Tom now that Joe is gone but not punished?
Is Hardy really finished with Broadchurch, or will something pull him back?

characters.name: Ellie Miller
characters.line: Detective and Joe's wife, publicly humiliated on the stand and estranged from her son Tom, but reconciled with Hardy as a partner.

characters.name: Alec Hardy
characters.line: Detective with a new pacemaker who has finally cracked Sandbrook and is preparing to leave Broadchurch, believing his penance is over.

characters.name: Joe Miller
characters.line: Danny's confessed killer, acquitted at trial and then forced out of town by the Latimers and Millers under threat if he ever returns.

characters.name: Beth Latimer
characters.line: Danny's mother, now with a newborn daughter Elizabeth, considering leaving Mark and left with no legal justice for her son.

characters.name: Mark Latimer
characters.line: Danny's father, his affair with Becca exposed in court, trying to rebuild the marriage while quietly grieving in secret meetings with a boy who reminds him of Danny.

characters.name: Jocelyn Knight
characters.line: Retired QC who prosecuted the Latimers' case and lost, hiding failing eyesight and a dying mother; reconciled with Maggie Radcliffe.

characters.name: Sharon Bishop
characters.line: Defence barrister and Knight's estranged protégée, who won Joe's acquittal and made peace with Knight at the end.

characters.name: Claire Ripley
characters.line: Sandbrook witness revealed as the real orchestrator of Pippa's murder, now arrested by Hardy.

characters.name: Lee Ashworth
characters.line: Claire's violent ex-husband, arrested for the Sandbrook killings after Ellie finds the bodies hidden under his floorboards.

characters.name: Paul Coates
characters.line: Local vicar dating Becca Fisher, who has been quietly counselling Joe and who brokered the beach-house confrontation that expelled him.
